paragraphs.title: Elkanah, His Two Wives, and the Journey to Shiloh

easy.q: What was the name of the man introduced at the beginning of the chapter?

easy.explanation: Elkanah had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah.
easy.q: How many wives did Elkanah have?

medium.explanation: He went to worship and sacrifice unto the Lord.
medium.q: What two things did Elkanah do when he went to Shiloh?

medium.explanation: Eli's sons were Hophni and Phinehas.
medium.q: Who were Eli's two sons serving at Shiloh?
What does “yearly” mean in this passage?

answers: He went yearly to worship and sacrifice
challenge.explanation: His yearly journey to worship and sacrifice shows regular devotion.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that Elkanah regularly worshipped the Lord?

answers: It was a place where priests served
challenge.explanation: The verse calls Hophni and Phinehas priests of the Lord at Shiloh.
challenge.q: What does the mention of Eli's sons indicate about Shiloh?

answers: Elkanah sacrificed, had children, and then reached Shiloh
Elkanah is introduced, his wives are named, and he goes to Shiloh
Eli blessed Hannah, and then Elkanah is introduced
challenge.explanation: The passage first introduces Elkanah, then his wives, and then his yearly journey.
challenge.q: Which sequence correctly describes the beginning of the story?

paragraphs.title: The Tension Between Hannah and Peninnah

easy.explanation: He gave portions to Peninnah, her sons, and her daughters.
easy.q: To whom did Elkanah give portions?

easy.explanation: Elkanah gave a worthy portion to Hannah.
easy.q: To whom did Elkanah give a worthy portion?

answers: She wept and did not eat
easy.explanation: Hannah wept and did not eat.
easy.q: What did Hannah do because of her distress?

medium.q: Why did Elkanah give Hannah a worthy portion?

medium.explanation: Peninnah provoked Hannah, and Hannah wept and did not eat.
medium.q: What did Peninnah cause Hannah to do?

answers: The other wife who opposed her
medium.explanation: Peninnah was Hannah's adversary and Elkanah's other wife.
medium.q: What does “her adversary” mean in this passage?

answers: Peninnah and her children received portions, while Hannah received a worthy portion out of love
Hannah and Peninnah received exactly equal portions
challenge.explanation: The distribution highlights Elkanah's special love for Hannah.
challenge.q: What contrast appears in the distribution of the portions?

answers: He did not speak to her
Her sorrow concerned having no children
challenge.explanation: His comfort did not remove her grief over being childless.
challenge.q: Why did Elkanah's words about being better than ten sons not remove Hannah's sorrow?

challenge.explanation: Peninnah provoked Hannah year after year.
challenge.q: What caused the continuing tension between Hannah and Peninnah?

easy.explanation: Hannah prayed unto the Lord and wept sore.
easy.q: What did Hannah do when she was in bitterness of soul?

easy.explanation: Hannah asked the Lord for a man child.
easy.q: What did Hannah ask for in her prayer?

easy.explanation: Eli thought Hannah had been drunken.
easy.q: What did Eli first think about Hannah?

answers: Give him unto the Lord all the days of his life
medium.explanation: She vowed to give him unto the Lord all his days.
medium.q: What did Hannah vow to do if she received a son?

answers: Her lips moved, but her voice was not heard
medium.explanation: Eli saw her lips move but did not hear her voice.
medium.q: Why did Eli think Hannah was drunken?

answers: A woman with a loud voice
medium.explanation: Hannah explained that she was sorrowful and troubled, not drunk.
medium.q: What does “a woman of a sorrowful spirit” communicate?

answers: Hannah prayed silently, but Eli mistook her behavior for drunkenness
Hannah sang loudly, but Eli ignored her
Hannah did not pray, and Eli prayed for her
challenge.explanation: Hannah prayed in her heart while only her lips moved, so Eli misunderstood her.
challenge.q: What is the difference between Hannah's prayer and Eli's interpretation of it?

answers: That she brought all her distress before the Lord
challenge.explanation: She describes pouring out her deepest sorrow in prayer.
challenge.q: What does Hannah emphasize by saying, “I have poured out my soul before the Lord”?

answers: He would stay home for one year
He would be given to Peninnah
He would be given unto the Lord all his days
challenge.explanation: Hannah vowed that the child would belong to the Lord all his life.
challenge.q: Which part of Hannah's vow concerned the whole life of the child?

paragraphs.title: Eli's Blessing and the Answered Prayer

answers: That the Lord would grant her request
That she would return to Peninnah
That she would go alone to Shiloh
easy.explanation: Eli prayed that God would grant her petition.
easy.q: What did Eli wish for Hannah?

answers: She ate, and her countenance was no more sad
easy.explanation: Hannah went her way, ate, and was no longer sad.
easy.q: How did Hannah change after Eli spoke to her?

easy.explanation: Hannah conceived and bare a son.

answers: She returned to eating with hope
medium.explanation: She ate, and her countenance was no more sad.
medium.q: What happened after Hannah received Eli's blessing?

answers: She had asked him of the Lord
medium.explanation: She said, “Because I have asked him of the Lord.”
medium.q: Why did Hannah call her son Samuel?

medium.explanation: Afterward Hannah conceived and gave birth to a son.
medium.q: What does “the Lord remembered her” mean in the story?

answers: The name recalls that Hannah asked him of the Lord
The name refers to Elkanah's home
The name refers to Eli's sons
challenge.explanation: Hannah named him Samuel because she had asked him of the Lord.
challenge.q: What connection exists between Samuel's name and Hannah's prayer?

answers: She continued to weep and did not eat
She ate again, and her countenance changed
challenge.explanation: Her renewed eating and changed countenance show restored hope.
challenge.q: What inward change is shown in Hannah after Eli's blessing?

answers: The blessing comes before the Lord grants Hannah's request
challenge.explanation: Eli blesses Hannah, and afterward the Lord grants her request.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between Eli's blessing and Samuel's birth?

paragraphs.title: Waiting for Weaning and Bringing Samuel to Shiloh

answers: She waited until the child was weaned
She did not want to worship the Lord
easy.explanation: Hannah waited until Samuel was weaned.
easy.q: Why did Hannah not go up with Elkanah after Samuel's birth?

easy.explanation: She brought three bullocks, flour, and a bottle of wine.
easy.q: What did Hannah bring to Shiloh with Samuel?

easy.explanation: She brought the child to Eli.
easy.q: To whom did Hannah bring Samuel?

answers: To nurse her son until he was weaned
medium.explanation: She remained to nurse Samuel until he was weaned.
medium.q: Why did Hannah remain at home?

answers: He told her to do what seemed good to her
He took Samuel to Shiloh by himself
medium.explanation: Elkanah said, “Do what seemeth thee good.”
medium.q: What did Elkanah say after Hannah explained her decision?

medium.explanation: The child was weaned when he no longer needed nursing.
medium.q: What does “weaned” mean in this passage?

answers: Hannah brought Samuel, then nursed him, and then decided to stay
Hannah waited for weaning, brought Samuel to Shiloh, and presented him to Eli
Eli brought Samuel, and then Hannah sacrificed
challenge.explanation: Hannah waited until Samuel was weaned before bringing him to Shiloh and Eli.
challenge.q: Which sequence of events is correct?

answers: He accepted her decision and encouraged her to keep her word
He did not know about Samuel
He forbade her to go to Shiloh
challenge.explanation: Elkanah accepted her plan and asked the Lord to establish His word.
challenge.q: What can be learned from Elkanah's response to Hannah?

answers: She had vowed to give him unto the Lord all his days
Samuel was one of Eli's sons
challenge.explanation: Hannah brought Samuel to the Lord as she had vowed.
challenge.q: Why was bringing Samuel to Shiloh connected with Hannah's vow?

paragraphs.title: Hannah Gives Samuel to the Lord

easy.q: To whom did Hannah speak when she brought Samuel?

answers: That she was the woman who had prayed there
easy.explanation: She reminded Eli that she was the woman who had prayed unto the Lord.
Hannah lent Samuel to the Lord all his days.
easy.q: To whom did Hannah give Samuel all his life?

answers: The Lord had given her the child she requested
medium.explanation: She said the Lord had given her the petition she asked of Him.
medium.q: What reason did Hannah give for giving Samuel to the Lord?

medium.explanation: She brings Samuel to the Lord as she had vowed.
medium.q: How do Hannah's words in this passage relate to her earlier prayer?

answers: I have taken him for myself
I have dedicated or given him to the Lord
medium.explanation: Hannah gives Samuel to the Lord for all his days.
medium.q: What does “I have lent him to the Lord” mean here?

answers: Samuel was named because Hannah asked him of the Lord, and she then lent him to the Lord
There is no connection between the name and Hannah's words
challenge.explanation: His name recalls Hannah's request, and her final words describe giving him to the Lord.
challenge.q: What verbal connection links Samuel's name with Hannah's final words?

answers: That bringing Samuel was the direct result of her prayer
That she had never truly prayed
That Eli had not been at Shiloh
challenge.explanation: She shows that Samuel was the answer to the prayer she made before Eli.
challenge.q: What does Hannah emphasize by reminding Eli of her earlier prayer?

answers: Request, answered prayer, and giving the child to the Lord
challenge.explanation: Hannah prayed for a son, received him, and gave him to the Lord as promised.
challenge.q: What is the main sequence of ideas in this passage?
